# One nonzero endpoint section: a formal obstruction and an actual segment constraint

This note distinguishes ordinary middle-section weights from full mixed critical section weights. It gives a precise obstruction to deriving the latter from middle cap fractions and chord-center bounds alone. It also proves a separate actual Minkowski containment obstruction for the limiting segment. It does not assert a realizable bad critical body or a quantitative finite-volume exclusion.

Use canonical normals v_1=(1,0),v_2=(0,1),v_3=(-1,-1), and

    T={x<=1,y<=1,x+y>=-1}, |T|=9/2.

## 1. Even three bisected middle chords do not determine the full weights

Let K=-T. At source 0 its three normalized section lengths are k_i=2; every chord is bisected at 0. Its three captured areas are q_i=2, so q_i/|K|=4/9<128/279 and the sorted profile equals |K| exactly:

    2+2+2/4=9/2.

Consider the FORMAL limiting endpoint-section array

    a_1=2, a_2=a_3=0.

Then s_i=k_i+2a_i=(6,2,2), t_i=a_i/s_i=(1/3,0,0), and the normalized full inverse weights are

    p=(1/7,3/7,3/7).

All middle chord centers are zero, so the inequalities k_i>=a_i and

    |c_i|<=a_i(k_i-a_i)/(k_i+2a_i)

hold. Thus these middle-body and scalar chord-center conditions alone do not force min p_i>=2/9, even when all three middle chords, rather than only two, are bisected. This is a formal array with zero limiting sections, not a body with three proper positive A sections and not a mixed critical counterexample.

## 2. A whole limiting segment is not the limit of a selected chord

For 0<e<1/4 let A_e be the actual triangle with vertices

    L_e=(-1-e,-1-2e),
    U_e=(-1-e,2+2e),
    P_e=(-1+2e,1/2).

All three cuts v_i.x=-1 are proper: x ranges across -1, y ranges across -1, and x+y ranges across 1. The area is

    |A_e|=(9/2)e+6e^2.

Its normalized sections at those lines are exactly

    sigma_A1=2+(8/3)e,
    sigma_A2=12e^2/(3+4e),
    sigma_A3=6e^2/(3-2e).                                   (1)

For the first expression, x=-1 occurs one third of the way from the vertical base to P_e; the two endpoint heights are -1/2-4e/3 and 3/2+4e/3. For the second, interpolate from L_e toward P_e until y=-1. For the third, interpolate from U_e toward P_e until x+y=1; the normalized diagonal length is its horizontal-coordinate difference because the Euclidean length and the normal length both acquire sqrt(2).

The bodies converge in Hausdorff distance to

    E=[(-1,-1),(-1,2)],

which has length three in the first normalized chord parameter. Yet the first selected proper chord lengths tend to two, not three. The other two selected sections tend to zero. This is an exact counterexample to silently identifying a surviving selected-section limit with the whole limiting segment. These triangles are not asserted compatible with K=-T and B=T or genuinely mixed critical.

## 3. A conditional limit lemma retaining the actual whole segment

Suppose A_j are planar convex bodies converging in Hausdorff distance to a compact convex set A_0 of dimension at most one. Assume all three fixed canonical cuts v_i.x=-1 are proper for every A_j, and

    liminf_j sigma_Aj,1>0.

Then A_0 is a nondegenerate segment on x=-1 and contains E.

Indeed the endpoints of the first cut chords remain in one compact set. A subsequence of their pairs converges to distinct points of A_0 on x=-1, because their lengths are bounded below. Thus A_0 has dimension one and lies on that line. Hausdorff convergence implies convergence of the minimum and maximum of each linear functional. Properness of the second and third cuts therefore implies that the limiting y range contains both -1 and 2. Convexity proves E subset A_0. This argument makes no assertion about convergence of the individual section lengths; Section 2 shows why none follows automatically.

For general fixed normals with determinant D and thresholds b_i satisfying sum b_i=-W<0, the analogous whole segment on v_1.x=b_1 connecting the other two cut lines has normalized length W/D. This follows in the coordinates (v_1.x,v_2.x), where its second coordinate runs from b_2 to -b_1-b_3=b_2+W, and normalized section lengths acquire the factor D.

## 4. The actual segment cannot coexist with the limiting equal-volume simplex configuration

Let B be a planar convex body contained in T, and let s>0. There is no configuration satisfying simultaneously

    |B|=s^2|T|,
    (E+B)/2 subset -sT.                                     (2)

To prove this, the three defining inequalities of -sT are x>=-s, y>=-s, x+y<=s. On E, the respective extrema are min x=-1, min y=-1 and max(x+y)=1. Consequently midpoint containment gives for every b in B

    b_x>=1-2s,
    b_y>=1-2s,
    b_x+b_y<=2s-1.                                          (3)

Writing h=2s-1, these inequalities are feasible for a full-dimensional B only if h>0. They say exactly B subset -hT. Hence the prescribed area in (2) gives s^2<=h^2, and positivity gives s<=h=2s-1, so s>=1. On the other hand B subset T and its prescribed area give s<=1. Thus s=1 and B has the full area of T while contained in T, forcing B=T: a proper closed convex subset of a convex body has strictly smaller area, by separation and an interior ball. But (3) would then also require T subset -T, which fails at the vertex (1,1). This contradiction proves the claim.

In particular the conditional limit in Section 3 is incompatible with a canonical middle simplex -sT, equal limiting B and K areas, and actual midpoint containment. The proof uses the whole limiting segment, not the generally discontinuous selected-section limit.

This final statement is conditional on the stated limit and exact limiting body data. It does not supply compactness for an arbitrary extremal sequence, prove that every sequence has this limit, or produce an explicit finite-a quantitative gap. Those would be separate required arguments before drawing any broader conclusion.

## 5. Equal cap volumes alone still allow an actual thin A with a short first section

There is also an exact actual-A obstruction to replacing the missing midpoint geometry merely by equality of the three endpoint cap volumes. Use the determinant-one coordinates

    xi=x+1, eta=y+x/2.

For positive H,e let A be the triangle whose apex is (xi,eta)=(-e/3,0) and whose base endpoints are (e,-H/2),(e,H/2). Its first canonical cap is xi>=0 and captures the fraction 15/16 of its area. Reflection eta -> -eta interchanges the second and third canonical cuts. The part missed by the second cap is a corner triangle of area fraction

    (H+e-3)^2/[2H(H+4e/3)],                               (4)

provided the displayed cut lies strictly between its lower vertex and the other two vertex levels. Thus all three captured areas equal 15|A|/16 whenever

    (H+e-3)^2=(H/8)(H+4e/3).                              (5)

An exact rational choice is

    H=375000/80987, e=711/80987.

In original coordinates the vertices are

    (-81224,40612)/80987,
    (-80276,-147362)/80987,
    (-80276,227638)/80987.

Each of the three cuts is proper. Direct rational clipping, independently of (4), gives

    a=177750000/6558894169,
    U_1=U_2=U_3=15a/16,
    sigma_A1=93750/80987,
    sigma_A2=sigma_A3=19750/4778233.

The first section is H/4, because xi=0 occurs one quarter of the way from the apex to the base. For the second section, interpolation gives

    sigma_A2=(4e/3)(H+e-3)/(H+4e/3),

and reflection gives the third. All are positive, and the first is strictly smaller than two.

With K=-T as in Section 1, the common formal raw menu budget is Q=2+15a/16 and the normalized full inverse weight of its first section is exactly

    p_1=4797983/25416949 < 2/9,
    2/9-p_1=7652051/228752541>0.

The other two full weights are equal and larger. The three middle chords remain bisected, the middle cap/profile constraints still hold, and all the scalar chord-center bounds hold because the centers vanish and every A section is at most its K section.

This is deliberately NOT a compatible bad mixed configuration. For B=T, the midpoint of the A apex and the B point (-2,1) has x=-121599/80987<-1, outside K=-T. Also its common menu budget exceeds the raw target for the three separate fibers by

    Q-(2/9)(a+|K|+|B|)=(103/144)a>0.

Thus equal endpoint cap volumes, fixed cut locations and the scalar chord bounds do not by themselves repair the needle-array argument. Actual midpoint containment and the target budget remain substantive constraints. The exact equal-middle-cap exclusion under badness is already contained in the archived joint cap-profile dispersion theorem; this example does not contradict it.

The actual triangles and all rational cap/section identities are independently checked by `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_bisected_chords_and_actual_needle_slab_recovery.py`; its combined 1,447 exact checks pass.
